doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Elvin's influence on rock drummers
summary: Brown argues Mitchell and Bonham carry Elvin's concept of time into rock; Elvin says no one had said this.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well that’s cause he knew how great you were. (Laughs) You were his hero! So when

Well, we talked about Mitch Mitchell, obviously because of his performing with Hendrix and because of Hendrix’s, in the rock world, phenomenal innovator, and great musician. But then behind Mitch Mitchell, there was also another drummer, John Bonham for Led Zeppelin. He definitely took your broke into (scats) and created his style after that. So between those two, Elvin Jones has permeated the entire rock drumming, rock music, from even before Mitch Mitchell, but definitely by the time Mitch Mitchell starts recording in1967 when John Bonham is playing Led Zeppelin everyone is playing Elvin Jones’ rhythm, Elvin Jones’ concept of time. Most people don’t understand that you’ve been filtered into these people, into the entire rock world! Most people who say, “I want to sound like Mitch Mitchell, I want to sound like John Bonham!” are really saying, “I want to sound like Elvin Jones” as far as I’m concerned. Has anyone talked to you about this experience, about how widespread your influence was in popular music, in rock music, not just jazz?

Well, you’re the first that I’ve talked to in that way. It’s just that people don’t talk about things like that. For some reason they don’t. If you know… I’m not acquainted with many drummers. They know me but I’ve never met ‘em so I can’t say I know the person. But if that…if it is rather… its flattering in a way and in a way its true, at least I hope so. If anybody can learn anything from what I do they’re welcome to it. (Laughs)
